# DensityClassifierFull { #dyf.DensityClassifierFull }

```python
DensityClassifierFull(
    embedding_dim=384,
    num_bits=14,
    seed=31,
    isolation_k=10,
    isolation_sample_size=1000,
    num_stability_seeds=3,
)
```

Density Classifier using PCA-based LSH.

Returns raw density metrics per item - classification is up to you.

## Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

>>> classifier = DensityClassifier(embedding_dim=384)
>>> classifier.fit(embeddings, categories=categories)
>>> print(classifier.report())
>>>
>>> # Get raw metrics
>>> labels = classifier.get_labels()
>>> sparse = labels.filter(pl.col('bucket_size') < 10)
>>> isolated = labels.filter(pl.col('isolation_score') > 0.5)

### fit { #dyf.DensityClassifierFull.fit }

```python
DensityClassifierFull.fit(
    embeddings,
    categories=None,
    texts=None,
    normalize=True,
    verbose=True,
)
```

Fit the density classifier.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name       | Type                                                                   | Description                        | Default    |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|------------|
| embeddings | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`)                               | (n, d) array of embedding vectors  | _required_ |
| categories | [Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[List](`typing.List`)\[[str](`str`)\]\] | Optional list of category labels   | `None`     |
| texts      | [Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[List](`typing.List`)\[[str](`str`)\]\] | Optional list of text content      | `None`     |
| normalize  | [bool](`bool`)                                                         | Whether to L2-normalize embeddings | `True`     |
| verbose    | [bool](`bool`)                                                         | Print progress                     | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                    | Description         |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|
|        | [DensityClassifier](`dyf.classifier.DensityClassifier`) | self (for chaining) |

### from_pandas { #dyf.DensityClassifierFull.from_pandas }

```python
DensityClassifierFull.from_pandas(
    df,
    embedding_col,
    category_col=None,
    text_col=None,
    **kwargs,
)
```

Create classifier from a Pandas DataFrame.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name          | Type                                           | Description                                               | Default    |
|---------------|------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| df            | [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | Pandas DataFrame with embeddings                          | _required_ |
| embedding_col | [str](`str`)                                   | Column name containing embedding vectors (list of floats) | _required_ |
| category_col  | [Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[str](`str`)\]  | Optional column name for category labels                  | `None`     |
| text_col      | [Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[str](`str`)\]  | Optional column name for text content (enables labeling)  | `None`     |
| **kwargs      |                                                | Additional args passed to __init__ (num_bits, seed, etc.) | `{}`       |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                    | Description                       |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
|        | [DensityClassifier](`dyf.classifier.DensityClassifier`) | Fitted DensityClassifier instance |

#### Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

>>> df = pd.read_parquet("embeddings.parquet")
>>> classifier = DensityClassifier.from_pandas(
...     df,
...     embedding_col="embedding",
...     category_col="category"
... )
>>> result = classifier.to_pandas()

### from_texts { #dyf.DensityClassifierFull.from_texts }

```python
DensityClassifierFull.from_texts(
    texts,
    categories=None,
    embedding_dim=128,
    max_features=10000,
    min_df=2,
    max_df=0.95,
    ngram_range=(1, 2),
    num_bits=12,
    verbose=True,
    **kwargs,
)
```

Create classifier from raw texts using TF-IDF + SVD embeddings.

No external embedding model required. Uses sklearn's TfidfVectorizer
and TruncatedSVD to create dense embeddings from text.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name          | Type                                                                   | Description                               | Default    |
|---------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|------------|
| texts         | [List](`typing.List`)\[[str](`str`)\]                                  | List of text documents                    | _required_ |
| categories    | [Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[List](`typing.List`)\[[str](`str`)\]\] | Optional category labels                  | `None`     |
| embedding_dim | [int](`int`)                                                           | SVD output dimensions (default 128)       | `128`      |
| max_features  | [int](`int`)                                                           | Max vocabulary size for TF-IDF            | `10000`    |
| min_df        | [int](`int`)                                                           | Min document frequency for terms          | `2`        |
| max_df        | [float](`float`)                                                       | Max document frequency for terms          | `0.95`     |
| ngram_range   | [Tuple](`typing.Tuple`)\[[int](`int`), [int](`int`)\]                  | N-gram range (default unigrams + bigrams) | `(1, 2)`   |
| num_bits      | [int](`int`)                                                           | Bits for PCA LSH                          | `12`       |
| verbose       | [bool](`bool`)                                                         | Print progress                            | `True`     |
| **kwargs      |                                                                        | Additional args passed to __init__        | `{}`       |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                    | Description                       |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
|        | [DensityClassifier](`dyf.classifier.DensityClassifier`) | Fitted DensityClassifier instance |

#### Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

>>> texts = ["doc about machine learning", "another ml paper", ...]
>>> classifier = DensityClassifier.from_texts(texts, categories=cats)
>>> print(classifier.report())

### get_labels { #dyf.DensityClassifierFull.get_labels }

```python
DensityClassifierFull.get_labels()
```

Get per-record labels as a Polars DataFrame.

#### Returns DataFrame with columns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns-dataframe-with-columns}

- index: Record index (0-based)
- bucket_id: Primary LSH bucket ID
- bucket_size: Number of items in same bucket
- centroid_similarity: Cosine similarity to bucket centroid
- isolation_score: How isolated the item is
- stability_score: How stable bucket assignment is (0-1)
- category: Category label if provided during fit

#### Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

>>> classifier.fit(embeddings, categories=categories)
>>> labels = classifier.get_labels()
>>> sparse = labels.filter(pl.col('bucket_size') < 10)

DensityClassifierFull.get_stability_scores()

### label_buckets { #dyf.DensityClassifierFull.label_buckets }

```python
DensityClassifierFull.label_buckets(
    base_url='http://localhost:11434/v1',
    model='qwen2.5:7b',
    samples_per_bucket=5,
    max_text_len=200,
    min_bucket_size=5,
    verbose=True,
)
```

Generate descriptive labels for buckets using a local LLM.

Uses OpenAI-compatible API (works with Ollama or MLX server).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name               | Type           | Description                                                 | Default                       |
|--------------------|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| base_url           | [str](`str`)   | API endpoint (Ollama: localhost:11434, MLX: localhost:8080) | `'http://localhost:11434/v1'` |
| model              | [str](`str`)   | Model name                                                  | `'qwen2.5:7b'`                |
| samples_per_bucket | [int](`int`)   | Number of representative texts to send                      | `5`                           |
| max_text_len       | [int](`int`)   | Max length of each sample text                              | `200`                         |
| min_bucket_size    | [int](`int`)   | Only label buckets with at least this many items            | `5`                           |
| verbose            | [bool](`bool`) | Print progress                                              | `True`                        |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                         | Description                                                                 |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [Dict](`typing.Dict`)\[[int](`int`), [Dict](`typing.Dict`)\] | Dict mapping bucket_id -> {'label': str, 'size': int, 'samples': List[str]} |

#### Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

>>> labels = classifier.label_buckets(
...     base_url="http://localhost:11434/v1",
...     model="qwen2.5:7b"
... )
>>> print(labels[1234]['label'])
'Reinforcement Learning'

### label_buckets_keywords { #dyf.DensityClassifierFull.label_buckets_keywords }

```python
DensityClassifierFull.label_buckets_keywords(
    top_k=3,
    min_bucket_size=5,
    stopwords=None,
    min_word_len=3,
    use_tfidf=True,
)
```

Generate labels for buckets using keyword extraction (no LLM required).

Extracts top keywords from bucket texts using TF-IDF or frequency analysis.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                          | Description                                      | Default   |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| top_k           | [int](`int`)                                  | Number of top keywords to include in label       | `3`       |
| min_bucket_size | [int](`int`)                                  | Only label buckets with at least this many items | `5`       |
| stopwords       | [Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[set](`set`)\] | Set of words to exclude (uses default if None)   | `None`    |
| min_word_len    | [int](`int`)                                  | Minimum word length to consider                  | `3`       |
| use_tfidf       | [bool](`bool`)                                | Use TF-IDF weighting (vs simple frequency)       | `True`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                         | Description                                                                                |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [Dict](`typing.Dict`)\[[int](`int`), [Dict](`typing.Dict`)\] | Dict mapping bucket_id -> {'label': str, 'keywords': List[Tuple[str, float]], 'size': int} |

#### Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

>>> labels = classifier.label_buckets_keywords()
>>> print(labels[1234]['label'])
'neural network training'
